beats.text: Okay, quick guess! Under thirty, who's more likely to be single? Men or women?
Here's the wild part. Most young men are single! Most young women? Not.
Pew Research asked over six thousand Americans about their love lives.
Under thirty, sixty-three percent of men are single! And the women? Not even close.
And it gets better. Among singles of all ages, half the men are looking. Only thirty-five percent of the women!
So if you're young, male and single? You're not behind. You're the majority!

sources: Pew Research Center (Feb 8, 2023), 'For Valentine's Day, 5 facts about single Americans'. Survey of 6,034 US adults, July 5-17, 2022. Single = not married, not living with a partner, not in a committed romantic relationship. Under 30: 63% of men vs 34% of women single (same in 2019). Among singles (all ages): 50% of men vs 35% of women looking for a relationship and/or dates. Via pewresearch.org.
